scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The small imported polygon lies in Plaquemines Parish. The modern community label is not verified as the precise identity or boundary of inhabitants in 1492. The narrative is explicitly grounded in documented community history.
Grand Bayou in Plaquemines is distinct from the Assumption Parish and Red River Parish places of the same name. Their childhood and industry histories are not used.
This community is not merged with the western Atakapa-Ishak map records. No simple language assignment or continuity from the historical Chawasha village of 1730 is inferred.
The research abstract was read, not the full 2011 paper. The imagery period is not a village founding date, and no unsourced land-loss percentage is added.
CRCL’s project records date the mound reef to 2021; the news story says 2022. The card attributes the project organization’s date and separates the 2024 residential reef.
The news source and AP syndication are one work. Their combined use is limited to the sacred-site identification and reported transfer, with no reproduced quotations or photos.
The mound’s construction date and exact archaeological composition were not established. It is not presented as an excavated or precisely dated prehistoric find.
No legislation, recognition status or prediction of unavoidable disappearance is asserted. Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
